catalog_card.title: Jeju Hydrangea Festival Tour: East Route
catalog_card.shortCardDescription: A seasonal small-group day-tour of east Jeju built around the island's hydrangea festivals (late May to mid-July, peak mid-June) at Hueree Natural Park and Ilchul Land. The route also covers two UNESCO World Heritage sites — Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak) and Seongeup Folk Village — plus Hamdeok Beach and the Micheon Cave lava tube. Hotel pickup in Jeju City, English/Chinese-speaking licensed guide-driver.

itineraryStops[0].name: Hotel pickup (Jeju City)
itineraryStops[0].description: **Pickup is consolidated across the four standard Jeju City pickup points** to keep the morning compact and the eastbound run-out clean: **Jeju International Airport (제주공항)** for guests with same-day arrivals or airport-area hotels (Hidden Cliff, Maison Glad, Lotte City, etc.); **Jeju City Hall (제주시청)** for the Yeon-dong / Nohyeong / Old Town hotel cluster; **Hagwi-dong (하귀동)** as the westernmost Jeju City pickup; and **Dongmun Traditional Market (동문시장)** for the eastern Jeju City Tapdong/Sarabong waterfront cluster. Sequence runs **Hagwi → Airport → City Hall → Dongmun → eastbound coastal route 1132** toward Hamdeok. The minicoach is **small-group (max ~14 pax)** with a licensed English-speaking guide. **Bilingual printed itinerary card** is distributed at first pickup, and the guide gives a weather brief plus a **hydrangea bloom-status read** (which gardens are at peak vs. early bloom that morning) so the photo-stop priorities can be calibrated for the day.

The west-to-east pickup ordering is intentional: it lets the coach pick up Hagwi guests first and use the remaining 25 minutes after Dongmun to reach Hamdeok in time for the morning beach tide window before busloads arrive.
itineraryStops[1].name: Hamdeok Seoubong Beach
itineraryStops[1].category: Coastal photo stop — emerald turquoise + Seoubong Oreum
itineraryStops[1].description: **Hamdeok Seoubong Beach (함덕 서우봉 해변)** is consistently ranked among **Jeju's top 3 beaches**, defined by the contrast between **white-sand beach (~500 m main stretch, 3 connected coves totaling ~900 m)** and the **adjacent volcanic cone Seoubong (서우봉, 'Cow Looking Like a Cow's Head' parasitic cone)** rising directly from the eastern end. The water's signature **emerald-turquoise color** comes from shallow coral-sand seabed reflecting through clear ocean — the Mediterranean-like contrast (rare in Korea) is what made Hamdeok one of the country's most photographed domestic beach destinations. The beach can absorb up to **50,000 daily visitors** at peak summer, but spring + autumn visits are typically uncrowded. **Seoubong Peak** (climbable ~1 hour to summit) wears **canola-yellow slopes in spring (March–April)** and offers a **panoramic eastward view to Manjanggul lava-tube area**. **Historical layer**: the sea cliffs immediately west of Seoubong hold **Imperial Japanese Army tunnels carved during WWII colonial occupation** — kamikaze suicide-boat shelters and ammunition stores, similar to the 18 caves at Seongsan Ilchulbong. The tunnels are publicly accessible (with signage explaining the historical context). The beach is the **central segment of Jeju Olle Trail Course 19 (조천 → 김녕)**, marked with the trail's signature blue-orange ribbons. **Cafe Delmoondo (델문도 카페)** anchors the beachfront — large terraces, sea-view, popular for Instagram and casual stops. **FREE admission**; the beach is **20 km / ~40-min drive from Jeju International Airport** on Route 1132.

itineraryStops[1].whyOnRoute: **Morning emerald + first hydrangea-route warmup.** Hamdeok is the first stop because of three deliberate east-route reasons. (1) **Tide + light timing**: arriving 09:30 catches the morning low-side tide window (most photogenic emerald-turquoise band before mid-morning swell + sun glare flatten contrast) — this is *the* signature Jeju east-coast photo, and getting it before the 10:30 coach-tour wave is a tangible guest win. (2) **Geographic anchor for the eastward arc**: Hamdeok sits ~14 km east of Jeju City on Route 1132 — the natural first pin on the coastal corridor that defines the day. Skipping it would force the day to either start with a 50-min highway run inland to Seongeup (visually dull) or open with a hydrangea garden (robbing the day of pacing variety). (3) **Hydrangea-route counterpoint**: Hamdeok's white sand + emerald water provides the day's only **non-floral** large-scenic anchor — every other substantive stop is hydrangea-coded or heritage-coded, so Hamdeok's role is to give the day visual breadth before the floral immersion.

itineraryStops[2].name: Seongeup Folk Village
itineraryStops[2].category: Joseon-era folk heritage — UNESCO/National Folklore designation
itineraryStops[2].description: **Seongeup Folk Village (성읍 민속마을)** is a **living Joseon-era walled town founded in 1423** during the reign of **Sejong the Great** as Jeong-eui-hyeon (정의현), one of the three administrative seats of Joseon-era Jeju. The village served continuously as a **county administrative center until 1914** — nearly **500 years** — and retains **110 traditional structures** today within the original eupseong (읍성) walled-town footprint, designed on **Korean feng shui principles** typical of Joseon county capitals. The entire village is designated **Important Folklore Cultural Heritage of South Korea**, with **multiple individual buildings** carrying separate heritage status. At the village center stand **two ancient trees designated Natural Monuments of South Korea** — a **Saw-leaf Zelkova (느티나무)** and a **Japanese Hackberry (팽나무)**, both estimated **600+ years old** and revered as the village's spiritual anchor. Historical scars are visible: a **major fire in 1826 destroyed ~80 buildings**, and the village suffered fire damage **during the Jeju Uprising in 1948** — both events preserved as historical record on village signage. The **peak household count (historical, pre-modern) was ~1,500** — today the village remains inhabited by ~250 families, many actively maintaining traditional crafts. Drama filming credit: **'Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace)' (MBC, 2003–2004)**, the international K-drama hit. Local specialty: **Omegisul (오메기술)** — a **rice-based traditional Jeju liquor** brewed by **one family for multiple generations**, with the brewing demonstrated and tasted free of charge at the home-brewery within the village. **FREE admission**; outdoor walking dominates (~70% outdoor / 30% indoor for individual hanok visits).

itineraryStops[2].whyOnRoute: **Heritage anchor and the day's only inland Joseon stop.** Three east-route reasons Seongeup belongs at 10:30. (1) **Geographic pivot**: Seongeup sits at the inland Pyoseon-myeon junction where the Hamdeok→Seongsan eastbound coastal arc detours south through the central highlands. Locking it as the morning's second substantive stop converts what would otherwise be 50 min of throughput driving into a heritage anchor with no detour penalty. (2) **Pace-and-tone counterpoint to the floral afternoon**: the rest of the day (Ilchul Land, Hueree) is hydrangea-immersive and garden-coded; Seongeup's stone-walled hanok lanes + pony-led Joseon administrative history give the route its only **deeply-cultural, unhurried walking** stop, preventing the day from collapsing into a floral-only photography tour. (3) **UNESCO-adjacent layer**: National Folklore Cultural Heritage No. 188 designation pairs naturally with the afternoon's UNESCO-triple Seongsan, building the east-route's heritage-plus-volcanism through-line that distinguishes it from the Tour 2 (southwest) garden-plus-coast variant.

itineraryStops[3].name: Lunch (local Jeju restaurant)
itineraryStops[3].description: **Lunch is at a local Jeju-style restaurant in the Pyoseon-myeon / east-Seongsan corridor**, selected from a rotating shortlist of 3 family-run establishments that the operator has vetted for **English-friendly menus, dietary accommodation (vegetarian + halal-friendly chicken/seafood options on request), and local Jeju specialties** at fair group pricing. Typical lunch options include **galchi-jorim (braised silver hairtail)**, **heuk-dwaeji bulgogi (Jeju black pork bulgogi)**, **bibimbap with seasonal namul**, and **maeun-tang (spicy fish stew)**. The exact restaurant is selected the day before based on group size, dietary requests, and kitchen availability — guests are notified of the venue at the morning briefing. **Lunch cost is at guests' own expense** (typically ₩12,000–₩18,000 per person) and is **not included** in the tour fee. Beverages and rice/banchan refills are always included with the meal regardless of which dish is ordered.

itineraryStops[4].name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
itineraryStops[4].category: UNESCO triple-designated tuff cone — climb to the rim
itineraryStops[4].description: **Seongsan Ilchulbong (성산일출봉, 'Sunrise Peak')** is a **5,000-year-old Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic tuff cone** — a rare landform created when an underwater basalt eruption broke the sea surface, the magma met seawater, and the resulting steam-explosive ash built a **182 m fortress-shaped crater** rim instead of a typical lava cone. The result is what UNESCO formally calls **'an exceptional example of an emergent Surtseyan-type volcanic edifice'**. The crater is **600 m wide × 90 m deep**, ringed by **99 jagged rim rocks** that local lore likens to a stone crown. Seongsan carries the **Triple UNESCO designation**: **World Natural Heritage (inscribed 2007-07-02)** as part of the **'Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes' property**, **Biosphere Reserve (2002)**, and **Global Geopark (2010-10)** — a stack matched only by Hallasan itself among Korean sites. **18 Imperial Japanese WWII caves** (kamikaze suicide-boat shelters, 1945) are tunneled into the seaward base. Trail: **0.8 km one-way, ~140 m elevation gain, 60 min round trip** on wide stone steps. **Haenyeo (해녀) demonstrations** run **daily at 13:30 and 15:00** at the rocky cove below the cone — Jeju women divers (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage 2016) descend without scuba gear. Admission updated **April 2025**: **Adult ₩5,000 / Youth+Child ₩2,500 / Group adult ₩1,600**, free under 7 and over 65. The summit deck is also part of the **Yeongjusipgyeong (Jeju 10 Scenic Wonders) canon**, and remains Korea's premier **annual New Year sunrise pilgrimage** destination — 50,000+ visitors ascend before dawn on January 1, with municipal sunrise-festival programming since 1995. **Udo Island (우도, 'Cow Island')** — Korea's largest secondary volcanic island — is clearly visible 4 km offshore from the summit, accessible by **15-min ferry from Seongsan Port** (₩10,500 round-trip) for guests with extra time on a different itinerary.

itineraryStops[4].whyOnRoute: **The day's UNESCO summit-anchor and east-route hero stop.** Three reasons Seongsan is the afternoon-1 anchor at 12:50. (1) **Triple-UNESCO weight**: Seongsan carries the only **simultaneous triple-designation** on the day's path — World Heritage (2007) + Global Geopark (2010) + Biosphere Reserve (2002). On a hydrangea-festival tour, this is the single biggest non-floral anchor and the stop that earns the tour its 'plus UNESCO' framing in catalog. (2) **Light + climb timing**: the 12:50–14:05 window post-lunch is optimal for the 25-min rim climb because guests are fresh-fueled but pre-mid-afternoon-heat (especially valuable in June hydrangea-season heat), and the early-afternoon south-southwest light flatters the tuff-cone's east-facing crater walls for photography. (3) **Pacing pivot for the floral finale**: Seongsan delivers the day's most physically engaged moment (climb), creating earned stillness for the gentler **Ilchul Land hydrangea preview** and **Hueree hydrangea finale** that follow — the route's deliberate geology-then-flowers narrative arc.

itineraryStops[5].name: Ilchul Land — Hydrangea Festival + Micheon Cave
itineraryStops[5].category: Hydrangea festival garden + lava-tube cave (June peak)
itineraryStops[5].description: **Ilchul Land (일출랜드)** is a **400,000 m² nature theme park** in Seongsan, opened **2002**, built around the **Micheon Cave (미천굴)** lava tube — a **1,700 m total length cave** with a **365 m artificially leveled walk-through section** open to visitors (~25-minute traverse). The cave is part of Jeju's **lava-tube system that shares geological lineage with Manjanggul Cave** — the UNESCO World Natural Heritage lava tube — and **functions as the operational alternate when Manjanggul closes for conservation maintenance or weather (typhoons, freezing)**. Where Manjanggul preserves its uneven natural floor as an authentic geological experience, Micheon's leveled walkway makes the cave **accessible to elderly visitors, families with strollers, and guests with mobility limitations** — a deliberate engineering choice that broadens the lava-tube experience to audiences who couldn't navigate Manjanggul. The interior is lit with **decorative seven-color lighting (gold, silver, bronze, red, black, blue, white)** highlighting cave formations — controversial among purists but practical for non-specialist tourist photography. Outside the cave, the park extends across **Subyeon Park, a reconstructed traditional Jeju village, Wild Flower Bonsai Garden, Cactus Greenhouse, Sculpture Street, and a Footbath Cafe (aroma foot spa)** — making this the **only Jeju attraction with an on-site Muslim prayer room** (a deliberate accessibility investment). Drama filming credit: **'Running Man' (런닝맨, SBS) Episode 89 (Alice-in-Wonderland themed, 2012)**. Admission: **Adult ₩12,000 / Youth ₩9,000 / Child ₩7,000**. Indoor/outdoor split is **30% indoor (cave + greenhouse)** / **70% outdoor (park grounds)** — meaningful for weather-flexibility planning.

itineraryStops[5].whyOnRoute: **The day's first hydrangea anchor — and the lava-tube counterpoint that gives the tour its 'flowers + geology' identity.** Three east-route reasons Ilchul Land sits at 14:30. (1) **Hydrangea-festival window**: Ilchul Land is one of the **top-4 Jeju hydrangea festival venues** alongside Hueree, Hallim Park, and Camellia Hill — and unlike pure botanical gardens, it pairs the floral festival with a **continuous-tour lava tube (Micheon Cave)**, producing the day's only garden-plus-geology compound stop. June visitors typically catch peak outdoor blooms here (peak window June 10–25) before the gentler late-afternoon Hueree viewing. (2) **Manjanggul alternate value**: Manjanggul is the famous Jeju lava tube but is closed for major periods of the year for conservation; Ilchul Land's Micheon Cave is the **operational alternate** that lets the east-route preserve a lava-tube experience year-round without depending on Manjanggul opening. (3) **Pace into Hueree**: Ilchul Land is a 70-min standing-walk garden — moderate intensity — sandwiching it between the high-effort Seongsan climb and the low-effort Hueree finale lets guests gradually decelerate into the day's photo-heavy floral close.
itineraryStops[6].name: Hueree Natural Park — Hydrangea highlight
itineraryStops[6].category: Hydrangea anchor + signature Jeju Black Pig Show
itineraryStops[6].description: **Hueree Natural Life Park (휴애리 자연생활공원)** is a year-round flower park on the southern foot of Hallasan, branded as **'an island within an island'** for compressing Jeju's seasonal flower calendar into a single, **Hallasan-backdropped** garden. The park rotates **five named festivals across the calendar year** — the **Plum Flower Festival** (mid-Feb to late March), the **Spring Hydrangea Festival** (early April through mid-June, indoor greenhouse + outdoor early bloomers), the **Summer Hydrangea Festival** (June peak through early July, outdoor full bloom), the **European Hydrangea Festival** (mid-July through August, distinct cultivars), the **Pink Muhly Festival** (mid-September through October), and the **Camellia Festival** (mid-November through January) — meaning **a tour visit lands inside a named active festival on roughly 320 days of the year**. **For the east-route hydrangea-festival tour, the June window catches the outdoor peak** with the **hydrangea greenhouse** as a guaranteed indoor refuge if afternoon thundershowers move in. The park's signature show is the **Jeju Black Pig Show**, scheduled four times daily at **11:00 / 13:00 / 15:00 / 17:00** — the 17:00 slot is the natural target for this tour's 15:50 arrival. **Jeju Black Pig is a designated Natural Monument of Korea**, and the show is the park's **most kid- and senior-friendly anchor** alongside the hydrangea walk. Other photo-zone draws include the **Jeju Cultural Village** (traditional games + thatched stone-walled hanok), the **insect exhibit hall**, the **wildflower garden**, and the **Hueree Cave** (a small neon-lit photo cave). The park is **~85% outdoor**, so the **hydrangea greenhouse + insect hall + Hueree Gallery Pang** serve as the day's late-afternoon weather-fallback options.

itineraryStops[6].whyOnRoute: **The day's hydrangea anchor and the floral finale that gives the entire tour its name.** Four reasons Hueree is the closing substantive stop at 15:50. (1) **Late-day light + hydrangea color**: Hueree's outdoor hydrangea fields face west-southwest with Hallasan as the visible horizon backdrop; the 15:50–17:05 window catches the **warm late-afternoon golden light** that makes hydrangea pinks and blues glow (midday flat light desaturates them). (2) **Black Pig Show timing**: the 17:00 show slot lines up exactly with the natural end-of-visit point — guests can do the garden walk first (15:50–16:30) and close on the show, instead of breaking up the garden flow to chase a midday show. (3) **Operational cushion**: Hueree's **~85% outdoor** profile makes it the day's biggest weather-exposed stop — placing it last (vs. opening with it) lets the guide see the afternoon weather develop and use the indoor greenhouse + insect hall + gallery as fallback if needed without rearranging the rest of the day. (4) **Tour identity completion**: this is the stop that completes the east-route's three-pillar identity — UNESCO triple (Seongsan) + Joseon heritage (Seongeup) + hydrangea festival anchor (Hueree). Closing on the anchor of the namesake festival is the route's earned narrative payoff.

routeShapeIntro.title: How this day flows
routeShapeIntro.subtitle: A seasonal east-Jeju loop built around the island's defining summer event. The hydrangea festivals at Hueree and Ilchul Land peak for roughly four weeks (late May to mid-July, peak mid-June) — narrow enough that most international travelers miss it without a planned tour. The route weaves the festival into the standard east-coast UNESCO circuit, so visitors who happen to be in Jeju during the bloom window get both the heritage day and the flowers in the same 9 hours.

whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[0].title: Why this route is built this way
whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[0].items: Jeju has four major hydrangea festivals (Hueree, Hallim Park, Camellia Hill, Ilchul Land). The east route includes two of them — Ilchul Land and Hueree — which together cover the broadest range of hydrangea varieties and photo settings. Pairing both is awkward by public bus.

Many seasonal flower tours skip heritage sites in favor of more flower stops. This route keeps Seongsan Ilchulbong and Seongeup Folk Village on the itinerary — meaning even if you don't care about hydrangeas, the day still earns its keep as a standard east-Jeju UNESCO loop.

Hydrangea bloom timing varies year to year by 1–2 weeks. If you arrive a bit early or a bit late in the season, the heritage stops still anchor the day. The guide will swap in the strongest available flower fields based on real-time bloom intel.
Hotel pickup beats self-driving for one-day visitors

Many Jeju visitors are 1–2-day stopovers from Seoul. Renting a car requires an International Driving Permit and 30+ minutes of paperwork at the airport. A guided 9-hour day with hotel pickup means you arrive, sleep, get picked up, and see the best of east Jeju — no driving stress on the volcanic ridge roads.

staticQuestions[0].question: When exactly do hydrangeas bloom on Jeju?
staticQuestions[0].answer: Typically late May to mid-July (peak mid-June), with peak around the last week of June. Bloom timing shifts ±1 week year to year based on spring rainfall and temperature. Check 1–2 weeks before your tour date for the latest update.
staticQuestions[1].question: Are admissions included?
staticQuestions[1].answer: No — budget about ₩30,000–₩40,000 per person for the day. Admissions: Seongsan Ilchulbong ₩5,000, Hueree ₩13,000, Ilchul Land ₩12,000, Seongeup Folk Village free.
staticQuestions[2].question: Why is Manjanggul closed?
staticQuestions[2].answer: Manjanggul Lava Tube is temporarily closed for safety repairs (status varies; check on booking date). The standard alternate is Micheon Cave at Ilchul Land, which is a similar lava-tube experience and is included in this route.
staticQuestions[3].question: How is this different from the West/South hydrangea tour?
staticQuestions[3].answer: This route covers Hueree + Ilchul Land hydrangeas plus east-coast UNESCO sites (Seongsan, Seongeup). The West/South tour (a comparable tour) covers Hallim Park + Camellia Hill hydrangeas plus south-coast sites (Cheonjeyeon Falls, Jusangjeolli cliffs). Choose the East if you want UNESCO peaks; the West if you want a denser concentration of flower gardens.
staticQuestions[4].question: Can I do this as a private tour?
staticQuestions[4].answer: The same operator runs a private version of the hydrangea tour with hotel pickup anywhere on Jeju and customizable timing. Different product page; ask for the private option if you're a group of 4+ or want pickup outside Jeju City without the +₩70,000 surcharge.
staticQuestions[5].question: Is this a good choice for first-time visitors to eastern Jeju?
staticQuestions[5].answer: Yes — it covers the most distinctive stops in the area in a single balanced day.
staticQuestions[6].question: Is the walking difficult?
staticQuestions[6].answer: An active day with several walking-heavy stops.
staticQuestions[7].question: Is this tour suitable for families?
staticQuestions[7].answer: Yes for families whose kids can handle a full day of moving around.
staticQuestions[8].question: Can older adults join comfortably?
staticQuestions[8].answer: Recommended only for active seniors comfortable with stairs and uneven ground.
staticQuestions[9].question: What's the recommended minimum age?
staticQuestions[9].answer: Best fit is around age 10 and up — children comfortable with a full-day rhythm and the walking notes above.
staticQuestions[10].question: Can the tour run in rainy weather?
staticQuestions[10].answer: Light rain is fine; heavy rain may change a few stops.

page_sections[4].props.itineraryStops[1]: A photo stop at one of Jeju's most loved beaches — emerald shallows, white sand, and dark basalt rocks. The small Seoubong volcanic cone rises directly from the eastern end of the beach.
Main attraction exploration with photo time
Featured anchor stop on this route — chosen for its cultural/scenic significance and fit with the day's pacing.
Open 24 hours (beach); managed swim season July–August with lifeguards
Easy — beach is flat sand; Seoubong hike is moderate (steps)
Public restrooms and shower facilities at beach

page_sections[4].props.itineraryStops[2]: A still-inhabited heritage village of stone-walled houses dating back centuries. The volcanic stone walls (dol-dam), thatched roofs, and traditional kitchens are the only place on Jeju where you can see the full pre-modern village layout intact. Listed as Korean Folklore Cultural Heritage.
Main attraction exploration with photo time

page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[2: Manjanggul Lava Tube is temporarily closed for safety repairs (status varies; check on booking date). The standard alternate is Micheon Cave at Ilchul Land, which is a similar lava-tube experience and is included in this route.
page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[3: How is this different from the West/South hydrangea tour?

This route covers Hueree + Ilchul Land hydrangeas plus east-coast UNESCO sites (Seongsan, Seongeup). The West/South tour (a comparable tour) covers Hallim Park + Camellia Hill hydrangeas plus south-coast sites (Cheonjeyeon Falls, Jusangjeolli cliffs). Choose the East if you want UNESCO peaks; the West if you want a denser concentration of flower gardens.
page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[4: Can I do this as a private tour?

The same operator runs a private version of the hydrangea tour with hotel pickup anywhere on Jeju and customizable timing. Different product page; ask for the private option if you're a group of 4+ or want pickup outside Jeju City without the +₩70,000 surcharge.
page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[5: Is this a good choice for first-time visitors to eastern Jeju?
Yes — it covers the most distinctive stops in the area in a single balanced day.

page_sections[9].props.staticQuestions[7: Is this tour suitable for families?
